([[Alpharetta, Georgia]]) | college = [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] (2015–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | career_end = | years1 = [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018–2019]] | team1 = [[Windy City Bulls]] | years2 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team2 = [[Maine Red Claws]] | years3 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team3 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years4 = 2021–2022 | team4 = [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] | years5 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team5 = Long Island Nets | years6 = {{nbay|2023|start}} | team6 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years7 = 2024–2025 | team7 = [[Joventut Badalona]] | years8 = 2025 | team8 = [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] | highlights = * [[Basketball Champions League|All-Champions League Defensive Team]] ([[2021–22 Basketball Champions League#Awards|2022]]) }} '''Kaiser Evan Bray-Gates''' (born November 8, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier Musketeers]]. ==High school career== Gates attended [[St. Francis Schools (Alpharetta, Georgia)|St. Francis High School]]. Alongside teammate [[Kobi Simmons]] and [[Malik Beasley]], he led the team to two, back to back, state titles. Gates finished with more than 1,200 points and is the school's all-time leading rebounder. He was regarded as three-star recruit and the 10th best player in Georgia by 247 sports and selected Xavier over offers from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] and [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite news |last1=Northam |first1=Mitchell |title=Alpharetta's Simmons and Gates will battle in Sweet 16 |url=https://www.myajc.com/news/local/alpharetta-simmons-and-gates-will-battle-sweet/WlNkTFRe1wf5sEGbuXrkUJ/ |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=March 22, 2017}} ==College career== Gates posted 3.2 points and 2.6 rebounds per game as a freshman. He missed the first five games of his sophomore season with a knee injury.{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Shannon |title=Star forward Kaiser Gates returns to Xavier University basketball |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/college-sports/xavier-university-sports/star-forward-kaiser-gates-returns-to-xavier-university-basketball |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |work=WCPO |date=November 25, 2016}} As a sophomore, Gates averaged 5.8 points and 4.1 rebounds per game and played an important role in Xavier's run to the Elite Eight.{{cite news |last1=Northam |first1=Mitchell |title=These former N. Fulton stars will be playing D1 hoops this year |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/local/these-former-fulton-stars-will-playing-hoops-this-year/yQzUmf7TeaU3YM6gkdLzgK/ |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=October 16, 2017}} In a win over Florida State in the Round of 32, he contributed 14 points, five rebounds and two assists. Gates averaged 7.2 points and 4.6 rebounds per game as a junior. He was a strong defender and shooter, hitting 37.8 percent of his three-point attempts.{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Xavier's Kaiser Gates hires an agent, staying in 2018 NBA Draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/05/xaviers-kaiser-gates-hires-an-agent-staying-in-2018-nba-draft/ |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 5, 2018}} Gates started 22 games as a junior, with most coming in the first half of the season. After the season, Gates declared for the NBA draft and hired an agent, thus forgoing his senior season at Xavier. He finished his career with 533 points.{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Patrick |title=Analysis: What Kaiser Gates' XU departure means for the Musketeers |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2018/05/08/kaiser-gates-foregoing-senior-year-xavier-basketball/584156002/ |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=May 8, 2018}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Gates signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] for NBA Summer League play. He averaged 6.7 points and 1.7 rebounds per game in three games. Gates signed a training camp contract with the Bulls on September 14, 2018.{{cite news |first=Dave|last=Clark|title=Report: Xavier's Kaiser Gates agrees to training-camp deal with Chicago Bulls|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2018/09/14/kaiser-gates-bulls-reportedly-agree-training-camp-deal/1306272002/ |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=October 5, 2018 |date=September 14, 2018}} He was waived by the Bulls on October 12, 2018.{{cite web |title=Bulls waive four players|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-four-players|website=NBA.com |accessdate=October 16, 2018 |date=October 12, 2018}} Gates was added to the training camp roster of the Bulls' G League affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web |title=WINDY CITY BULLS RELEASE 2018–19 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-release-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=October 22, 2018 |date=October 21, 2018}} On October 18, 2019, the Celtics waived Gates.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/10/celtics-release-kaiser-gates.html|title=Celtics Release Kaiser Gates}} Gates played in all 50 of Windy City's games, averaging 12.7 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. On September 12, 2019, his returning rights were traded to the [[Maine Red Claws]] for the #4 overall pick in the 2019 G League draft.{{cite news |title= Red Claws Acquire Rights To Kaiser Gates |url= https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/red-claws-kaiser-gates/ |accessdate= November 3, 2019 |work= [[NBA.com]] |date= September 12, 2019 |archive-date= September 9, 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210909103705/https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/red-claws-kaiser-gates/ |url-status= dead }} On January 9, 2020, Gates finished with 24 points and 10 rebounds and made a buzzer-beating game-winning layup in a 120–118 triple overtime win over the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=Kaiser Gates, former Xavier player, beats buzzer for G League's Maine Red Claws |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/01/10/kaiser-gates-makes-buzzer-beater-maine-red-claws-nba-g-league/4432795002/ |accessdate=January 10, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=January 10, 2020}} On December 16, 2020, Gates was signed by the [[Brooklyn Nets]],{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Elie Okobo and Kaiser Gates |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/12/16/brooklyn-nets-sign-elie-okobo-and-kaiser-gates |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=December 16, 2020}} and was then waived the next day.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Kaiser Gates |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/12/17/brooklyn-nets-waive-kaiser-gates |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=December 17, 2020}} On January 27, 2021, Gates was included in the roster of the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-2021-roster|date=January 27, 2021|website=NBA.com |access-date=January 27, 2021}} In 12 games, Gates averaged 9 points and 5.7 rebounds per game. On September 8, 2021, Gates signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite news |title=Kaiser Gates joins Hapoel Jerusalem |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kaiser-gates-joins-hapoel-jerusalem/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 9, 2021 |date=September 9, 2021}} On November 4, 2022, Gates was named to the opening night roster for the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Complete 2022-23 Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-complete-2022-23-roster/n-5895915|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} On September 30, 2023, Gates signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]],{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign six players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-roster-six-players-signed-2023-2024-nba-season|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} but was waived on November 3.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Jeremiah Robinson-Earl|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jeremiah-robinson-earl-signed-pelicans-roster-110323|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2023|access-date=November 3, 2023}} On November 12, 2023, Gates rejoined the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite tweet|author=NetsDaily|title=The 6’7” SF Kaiser Gates who’s played last two years for Long Island Nets and was cut by the Pelicans two weeks ago is back on the Island, signing with Nets affiliate who had a roster opening. Per Hoopshype’s Alberto de Roa.|number=1723676896351670710|user=NetsDaily|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} On July 26, 2024, Gates signed with [[Joventut Badalona]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=Kaiser Gates: un aler pivot polivalent amb molt bon 2024|language=Catalan}} On January 20, 2025, Gates signed with [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] until the end of the [[2024-25 ACB season|2024-25 season]], with a one-year extension
